newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ELECTROLUX TO CUT COSTS FURTHER - MAGAZINE.
newsitem.headline: ELECTROLUX TO CUT COSTS FURTHER - MAGAZINE.

text.p: Swedish appliance maker Electrolux will have to cut its costs significantly even after seeing through the current restructuring programme, Swedish business weekly Veckans Affarer reported on Monday.
"The (restructuring programme) is a one-time cost cut which we have to do immediately," Electrolux chief executive Michael Treschow told the weekly in an interview.
"In the longer term we will surely be forced to reduce costs much more as consumers just aren't willing to pay more for the goods."

Veckans Affarer estimates the announced programme -- which involves slashing 12,000 of 100,000 jobs, shutting down 25 plants and 50 storage sites -- will give cost savings of 3-3.5 billion crowns and an operating margin of 6.5-7.0 percent.
"Of course we have calculated a bit high. We know that we cannot retrieve every crown," Treschow told the weekly.
Treschow also repeated the company's longterm efforts on the U.S. market.

"There were expectations about me making a decision to leave the U.S. market. But that would have been a large failure and meant that we would have been forced to give up our global strategy," he was quoted as saying.
